tidygenclust

tidygenclust provides functions and methods to run genetic clustering in R, and to align and compare multiple runs of the same or different K. tidygenclust builds on tidypopgen, enhancing the grammar of population genetics with a focus on genetic clustering.

Its core functionality is provided by native R and C++ code:

  • gt_radmix() to estimate ancestry proportions with the method of ADMIXTURE (Alexander et al. 2009). It is a heavily optimized, multithreaded C++ implementation of the algorithm of ADMIXTURE (block relaxation with quasi-Newton acceleration), which works directly on a gen_tibble, supports pseudohaploid data, and includes the cross-validation of ADMIXTURE to choose K (Alexander & Lange 2011). Its code started as a port of OpenADMIXTURE.jl (Ko et al. 2023) and has since been extensively rewritten; its optional SVD start adapts the alternating least squares of ADAMIXTURE;
  • gt_clumppling() to align multiple clustering runs within and across K with the method of clumppling (Liu, Kopelman & Rosenberg 2024), ported to R and C++, with modifications, from the python package clumppling.

Optionally, on Linux, tidygenclust can also run the python packages fastmixture (gt_fastmixture()) and ADAMIXTURE (gt_adamixture()), and the original ADMIXTURE program (tidypopgen::gt_admixture()), which it installs in a conda environment on request.

Installation

You can install the development version of tidygenclust from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("EvolEcolGroup/tidygenclust")

gt_radmix() and gt_clumppling() work straight away. The optional tools (fastmixture, ADMIXTURE and ADAMIXTURE) are installed with reticulate in a conda environment, ctidygenclust, when you ask for them (this only works on Linux at the moment: on Windows, you can use them through the WSL; on macOS, they are not available, as their OpenMP library conflicts with that of R).

Overview of functionality

An overview of the functionality of tidygenclust and its integration with tidypopgen is provided in the “Get Started” vignette. This also includes a detailed description of how to align multiple runs of clustering and compare them. There are also several articles in the “Articles” section of the website of the package:

  1. Benchmarking gt_radmix() against ADMIXTURE, fastmixture and ADAMIXTURE.

  2. Benchmarking gt_clumppling() against the python clumppling.

  3. Installing and running external tools.

  4. An illustration of how treating pseudohaploids as if they were diploids can bias the results of clustering (and how gt_radmix() can handle pseudohaploids correctly).

The website documents the version on the main branch; the documentation of the development version, on the dev branch, is at https://evolecolgroup.github.io/tidygenclust/dev/.

References

Alexander DH, Novembre J, Lange K (2009) Fast model-based estimation of ancestry in unrelated individuals. Genome Research, 19(9), 1655-1664.

Alexander DH, Lange K (2011) Enhancements to the ADMIXTURE algorithm for individual ancestry estimation. BMC Bioinformatics, 12, 246.

Ko S, Chu BB, Peterson D, Okenwa C, Papp JC, Alexander DH, Sobel EM, Zhou H, Lange KL (2023) Unsupervised discovery of ancestry-informative markers and genetic admixture proportions in biobank-scale datasets. The American Journal of Human Genetics, 110(2), 314-325.

Liu X, Kopelman NM, Rosenberg NA (2024) Clumppling: cluster matching and permutation program with integer linear programming. Bioinformatics, 40(1), btad751.
